Simulate networks from a fitted AME model

Source: R/simulate.ame.R
simulate.ame.Rd

Generates networks from aligned joint posterior draws. A fit that did not save them can use the conditional approximation by asking for it with type = "approximate"; see Details.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ame'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 100,
  seed = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  burn_in = 0,
  thin = 1,
  return_latent = FALSE,
  type = c("posterior", "approximate"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

fitted model object of class "ame"

nsim

number of networks to simulate (default: 100)

seed

Optional random seed. An explicit seed is local to this call: the caller's RNG state is restored on return or error. With NULL, the caller's current RNG stream advances normally.

newdata

optional list containing new covariate data:

Xdyad

dyadic covariates (n x n x p array or nA x nB x p for bipartite)

Xrow

row/sender covariates (n x p matrix or nA x p for bipartite)

Xcol

column/receiver covariates (n x p matrix or nB x p for bipartite)

If NULL, uses covariates from original model fit

burn_in

number of initial MCMC samples to discard (default: 0, assumes burn-in already removed)

thin

thinning interval for MCMC samples (default: 1, use every sample)

return_latent

logical: return latent Z matrices in addition to Y? (default: FALSE)

type

simulation route: "posterior" (default) replicates the network from aligned saved posterior draws; "approximate" is the conditional approximation. See Details.

...

additional arguments (not currently used)

Value

A list with components:

Y

list of nsim simulated networks in the same format as the original data

method

joint posterior or conditional approximation

draw_index

sampled coefficient-row indices for joint replication

Z

if return_latent=TRUE, list of nsim latent Z matrices

family

the family of the model (binary, normal, etc.)

mode

network mode (unipartite or bipartite)

Details

With type = "posterior", every replicate uses the same saved MCMC iteration for coefficients, actor effects, positions, coupling and observation variance. Saved blocks may be thinned differently when their iteration indices are available; only shared iterations are sampled. Missing joint storage is an error (class lame_simulate_draws) that names type = "approximate". Store effects and positions with posterior_options(save_ab = TRUE, save_UV = TRUE, thin_ab = 1, thin_UV = 1) when fitting.

type = "approximate" is the conditional approximation: it substitutes posterior summaries for the latent trajectories and does not propagate their joint posterior uncertainty. It runs only when requested. The returned method identifies the route.

Ordinal fits with explicit cutpoints use the corresponding saved cutpoint draw. Data-induced ordinal fits match the observed category frequencies, so these replications assess dependence conditional on those frequencies.

Author

Cassy Dorff, Shahryar Minhas, Tosin Salau

Examples

# \donttest{
# Fit a model
data(YX_bin)
# chains = 1 keeps the example short; the default runs two chains and compares them
fit <- ame(YX_bin$Y, Xdyad = YX_bin$X, burn = 50, nscan = 250, odens = 5,
           family = "binary", verbose = FALSE,
           posterior_opts = posterior_options(save_ab = TRUE, save_UV = TRUE), chains = 1)

# Simulate 10 networks from posterior
sims <- simulate(fit, nsim = 10)
# }
